To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expression of the more compliant N-terminal titin isoform (N2BA) was increased in the failing human heart and that this increase in titin isoforms was correlated with reduced myocardial stiffness and improved diastolic filling.
titin expression is changed in patients with dilated cardio-myopathy and that the changes in expression affect LV stiffness and function.
titin isoforms are altered in dilated cardiomyopathies, which leads to a reduction in passive myocardial stiffness and a change in left ventricular filling pattern.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular basis of heart failure.
the molecular mechanisms of cardiac hypertrophy and failure, in particular with the giant sarcomeric protein titin and its regulatory elements.
the role of titin isoform switching in the development of heart failure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
titin isoforms are important determinants of myocardial stiffness in heart failure and, therefore, play an important role in diastolic function.

the altered titin expression, myocardial stiffness, and left ventricular function in patients with dilated cardiomypathy is a very interesting topic for research and further studies are necessary to clarify the role of titin in heart failure.
titin is not a major determinant of the contractile apparatus in heart failure, and that it is unlikely that titin will be an important therapeutic target.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the altered isoform expression in patients with dilated cardio-myopathy significantly impacts LV function by lowering myocardial stiff-ness and that this might extend to cell signalling and regulation of gene ex-pression.

the expression of N2BA isoforms of titin is increased in patients with end stage heart failure and that this is accompanied by increased expression of the titin-binding protein ankrd2 and diabetes ankyring protein.

the titin protein is a major determinant of myocardial passive tension in the heart, that it is upregulated in the failing heart, and that it plays a role in the regulation of myocardial contractility.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the more compliant titin isoform, N2BA, was upregulated in end-stage heart failure patients with nonischemic, dilated cardiomyopathies.
the more compliant N-2BA isoform of the giant protein, titin, is upregulated in end-stage dilated cardiomyopathic hearts.
titin expression changes in heart failure patients.
